relation_text_en:
Members' recommended course - traditional hanok village / Traditional Concept - Bukchon ‘s sloping lanes are filmed in BTS Suga’s “Daechwita,” IU’s hanbok-themed videos, and many traditional-concept comebacks. The famous Bukchon-ro 11-gil hanok view appears in K-drama OSTs.
The money shot is the view down Bukchon-ro 11-gil , tiled hanok roofs stacking toward the downtown towers — you’ll have seen it in traditional-concept comebacks and countless drama OSTs. Remember this is a living residential neighborhood: signs ask visitors to keep quiet and photograph before 17:00, and residents genuinely appreciate it. Go early morning for empty lanes.

relation_text_ko: 조선 왕조의 정궁으로, 방탄소년단 'Idol'의 궁궐 컨셉 비주얼, 슈가 솔로 작업, 아이유의 한복 컨셉 촬영, 블랙핑크 'How You Like That'의 전통 궁중 의상 장면 등에 반복적으로 등장. 광화문·흥례문·근정전이 주로 사용됨
relation_text_en:
Joseon dynasty royal palace / Royal Backdrop - Gyeongbokgung has been featured in BTS “Idol” (palace-themed visuals), Suga’s solo work, IU’s traditional concept shoots, and BLACKPINK’s “How You Like That” with traditional Korean court costumes. The Gwanghwamun gate, Heungnyemun, and Geunjeongjeon throne hall are repeatedly used.
Rent a hanbok from a shop near Exit 5 (around ₩15,000 for four hours) and you walk in free — the same traditional-concept look idols wear in palace shoots, and by far the best value photo op in the city. Aim for the 10:00 opening or the last hour before close to dodge tour groups, and don’t miss the changing-of-the-guard ceremony at Gwanghwamun gate. The palace is the anchor of Seoul’s historic core; our things to do in Seoul guide slots it into a wider day.

relation_text_en:
The Sci-Fi Backdrop - Designed by architect Zaha Hadid, DDP has appeared in BTS music videos, ATEEZ comebacks, NCT 127’s stage backdrops, and dozens of music-show award sets. The reflective silver paneling and undulating curves are unmistakable.
Come at dusk. DDP is engineered for night — the seamless aluminum panels catch the last light, then the LED rose garden on the north lawn switches on and the whole plaza turns into a photo set. The exterior ramps and the “future path” tunnel are the two angles you’ll recognize instantly from award-show and MV backdrops; both are free and open 24 hours. Weekday mornings are near-empty if you want clean shots without crowds. It sits right on the Dongdaemun night-shopping strip, so pair it with a late browse and a snack from the market stalls.

The 555-meter Lotte World Tower appears in many recent music videos as the night-skyline icon. Seoul Sky observatory shots are common (BTS, aespa, ITZY).
Even if you skip the paid observatory, the tower reads as “Seoul at night” in dozens of videos, and the Seokchon Lake at its base — cherry blossoms in spring, ringed by Lotte World rides — is a free and far prettier photo spot. Jamsil Exit 1 drops you between the tower, the lake, and the theme park.
